title: Simple past
subtitle: werkte, woonde, liep, was, had, kon: stories and descriptions in the past

explain.text: The **simple past** (*verleden tijd*) of a regular verb is the **stem + -te** or **stem + -de**. Use the same 't kofschip rule as for the participle: the letter before *-en* is t, k, f, s, ch or p → **-te**; any other letter → **-de**.

explain.nl: Ik werkte vroeger in een restaurant.
explain.en: I used to work in a restaurant.

explain.nl: Wij woonden drie jaar in Delft.
explain.en: We lived in Delft for three years.

explain.text: In the **singular** all persons have the same form (*ik, jij, hij werkte*). In the **plural** add **-n** (*wij werkten*). If the stem already ends in **t** or **d**: *wachten → wachtte(n)*, *antwoorden → antwoordde(n)*.

items.explain: The k of werken is in 't kofschip: -te.
The stem wacht ends in t, so add -te.

explain.text: **Strong verbs** change their vowel in the past: *lopen → liep*. There are no endings in the singular (*ik liep, hij liep*). In the plural add **-en** (*wij liepen*). Often the vowel also changes between singular and plural: *ik at, wij aten*; *ik las, wij lazen*.

explain.nl: Gisteren at ik een broodje met kaas.
explain.en: Yesterday I ate a cheese sandwich.

explain.nl: Wij aten laat en wij dronken thee.
explain.en: We ate late and drank tea.

explain.text: Some verbs have a mix: *kopen → kocht(en)*, *denken → dacht(en)*, *brengen → bracht(en)*, *weten → wist(en)*. They look regular but have a different vowel or consonant. Learn them as pairs.

explain.text: These very common verbs are almost always used in the simple past, even in speech: **zijn → was/waren**, **hebben → had/hadden**, and the modals **kunnen → kon/konden**, **moeten → moest/moesten**, **willen → wilde(n) / wou(den)**, **mogen → mocht(en)**. Also **gaan → ging/gingen**, **komen → kwam/kwamen**, **doen → deed/deden**, **zeggen → zei/zeiden**.

explain.nl: Gisteren was ik ziek en ik kon niet werken.
explain.en: Yesterday I was ill and could not work.

explain.nl: Wij hadden vroeger een grote tuin.
explain.en: We used to have a big garden.

explain.text: A modal stays in the second place and the infinitive goes to the end: *Ik moest gisteren werken.*

explain.text: Dutch uses both tenses and the difference is small. A simple rule that works: use the **perfect** for a **single finished event** in conversation (*Gisteren heb ik gewerkt*). Use the **simple past** to **describe** a situation, to tell a **story**, for **habits** in the past, and for **was, had** and the **modals**.

explain.text: Do not mix tenses without a reason. In a short story keep one tense: *Ik stond op, ik ontbeet en ik ging naar mijn werk.*
